title: Chairs
tagline: A training programme in how a committee actually works, argued from primary sources.
description: The Advanced Diplomat Cohort programme: Rules of Procedure, Effective Communication, Design Thinking, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Major Events, and Company Portfolio research.

modules.title: Rules of Procedure
modules.outcome: Run a committee session under the written rules: motions, points, yields, documents and voting.
modules.note: This module is procedure, not strategy. Every rule line is tagged to the Diplomathon page it comes from; the four closing slides complete the guide's sections on precedence, working papers, resolutions and clause language.

modules.title: Effective Communication
modules.outcome: Deliver a 90-second speech a room can follow, and listen well enough to answer it.
modules.note: Communication is treated as a two-way act: what you send, what the room receives, and the assumptions that turn an observation into a belief.

modules.title: Design Thinking
modules.outcome: Turn an agenda into one defined problem and a solution tested against real users.
modules.note: The five phases are iterative, not a checklist. The group challenges at the end force a return to an earlier phase, which is the point of the method.

modules.title: Entrepreneurship & Innovation
modules.outcome: Test whether a solution can be funded, run and grown, then argue the case for it.
modules.note: Entrepreneurship here covers value created inside an existing domain as well as a new enterprise. Creativity, feasibility and impact are assessed together.

modules.title: Major Events That Changed the World
modules.outcome: Argue from precedent, with dates and consequences that survive a challenge.
modules.note: Ten events, one seven-part frame. The module rewards the delegate who can compare two events without flattening either of them.
sources: Major Events that Changes the World.pdf p.1–3

modules.title: Company Portfolio
modules.outcome: Research a company portfolio to primary-source standard, then defend it in the room.
modules.note: The method is the same spine as a country portfolio; the evidence base changes. Worked portfolios and a source hierarchy make the method concrete.
sources: Research Sources for Company Portfolios p.1–4

library.title: Portfolio Library
library.note: Eleven portfolios across seven committees. Each entry carries the sources to cite and the laws that constrain it. This is reference material, not a taught module.
sources: Research Sources for Company Portfolios p.1–4
library.citation: Cite the company's own reports first, then the regulators and global bodies for its industry. Company or body, Title, Year, page or section, URL. News outlets such as Reuters, the FT and Bloomberg count as secondary.
